questions.question: Confirm the Java version for the legacy monolith.
questions.rationale: The README and request specify Java 8.

options.label: Java 8
options.description: Use Java 8 for the build and runtime.

questions.question: Confirm the framework for the single deployable application.
questions.rationale: Use one Spring Boot application to serve the browser pages and connect to Oracle. Do not deploy a separate frontend or API service.

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: A serverless option; not part of this on-premises legacy demo.

questions.question: Confirm Oracle Database as the datastore for the legacy demo.
questions.rationale: Use Oracle for the legacy application. PostgreSQL migration is future work.

options.label: Oracle Database
options.description: Use a real Oracle schema. Recommended: Oracle AI Database Free in a local Linux container with a persistent volume. Alternatives: a native or VM install, or an existing on-premises Oracle instance. A local Free edition demo does not represent a production license.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Does not meet the stated demo scope.

questions.question: Should operators sign in to use the application?
questions.rationale: The approved extension requires a presenter account stored in Oracle and sign-in for all application pages. No public registration or per-employee accounts.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require operators to sign in before they can use the dashboard.

options.label: No
options.description: Keep the demo local to the presenter’s machine without a sign-in screen.

questions.question: Confirm or change the defaults. Should the dashboard be a browser-based intranet UI with keyboard navigation, visible focus, and status text as well as color? Will viewers use it only on the presenter's PC or also from other machines? Is manual, read-only investigation enough, or should operators be able to save notes, acknowledge alarms, or record readiness checks? Should those edits persist across restarts, and do you need a reset for repeat demos? Is Docker Desktop with Linux containers acceptable, or should the demo connect to a native install, a VM, or an existing Oracle instance? Should the demo use both amber and green status accents, or favor one?
questions.header: Dashboard, operator workflow, and local setup
questions.answer: Use a keyboard-accessible desktop browser dashboard, local to the presenter by default. Add an overview home page with plant and line totals, upcoming maintenance, and shift summaries. Keep the four-plant, 160-line register and manual line investigation. Add read-only scheduled maintenance and maintenance history by line. Add a read-only rota for fictional employees, filtered by plant, date, and shift. Require presenter sign-in for all application pages, using an Oracle user table with hashed passwords and browser sessions; create one presenter account during setup and do not provide public registration. Store all fictional records in the existing Oracle Free database with a named volume. Preserve the cream background, deep red tab navigation, white table panels, muted amber warnings, and muted green healthy statuses with text labels. No operator writes, PLC connection, AI, migration, or Azure deployment.
questions.rationale: These choices determine local setup, accessibility, and whether the app needs to write operator data. Keep the 2008-era intranet look and leave AI, Azure deployment, and database migration out of scope.
questions.recommendedChoice: Use a keyboard-accessible desktop browser dashboard, local to the presenter by default. Show four plants and 160 fictional lines with plant and status filters. The line detail shows a short alarm history, last recorded equipment signals, readiness checks, and fictional manual excerpts rendered as text. Use a read-only manual investigation flow with a repeatable dataset stored in Oracle; no PLC or other equipment connection. Use a local Oracle Free container with a named volume. Use a cream background, deep red navigation, white table panels, muted amber warnings, and muted green healthy statuses; pair each color with a text label.
